comparisons.peer_summary: Global Transaction Services revenue decreased by $911 million in 2024 compared to 2023, primarily due to higher deposit costs, partially offset by higher average deposit balances and treasury service charges.
comparisons.comparison: Both Goldman Sachs (GS) and Bank of America (BAC) report that their respective transactional or platform banking revenues were negatively impacted by higher deposit costs, which were partially offset by the benefit of higher average deposit balances. GS attributes its lower Transaction Banking revenue specifically to the sale of a seller financing loan portfolio, while BAC attributes its Global Transaction Services revenue decline primarily to deposit cost increases.

sentences.text: Transaction banking and other net revenues were lower, primarily reflecting lower net revenues related to the seller financing loan portfolio that was sold during 2024.

Global Transaction Services revenue decreased $911 million in 2024 compared to 2023 primarily driven by higher deposit costs, partially offset by the benefit of higher average deposit balances and treasury service charges.

comparisons.peer_summary: Retail Banking revenues decreased 1% due to the transfer of certain relationships and associated deposit balances to Wealth, partially offset by higher deposit spreads and loan growth, with average mortgage loans up 15% and average deposits down 17% ($17 billion transferred).
comparisons.comparison: Both GS and Citigroup (C) highlight the tension between balance volume drivers and strategic structural changes in their platform/revenue discussions. GS notes that higher average credit card and deposit balances in Consumer platforms were largely offset by the transition of the GM credit card program (a strategic/counterparty change). Similarly, C notes that Retail Banking revenues were driven down by the transfer of deposit balances to Wealth, partially offset by growth in loan products. Both disclosures detail specific balance sheet movements (transfers/transitions) that offset underlying volume growth.

sentences.text: Notwithstanding our strategic decision to narrow the focus on consumer-related activities, Consumer platforms net revenues were slightly higher compared with 2023, reflecting higher average credit card balances and higher average deposit balances, largely offset by the impact of the planned transition of the GM credit card program to another issuer.

Retail Banking revenues decreased 1%, driven by the impact of the transfers of certain relationships and the associated deposit balances to Wealth, partially offset by higher deposit spreads, as well as mortgage and installment loan growth.
Average deposits decreased 17%, largely reflecting the transfer of certain relationships and the associated deposit balances to Wealth ($17 billion at the time of transfer over the last 12 months).
